title: Conormal relations vanish in resolution homology
statement: For A, I and n and a projective resolution P of A/I, specify an augmentation-preserving Koszul chain map a(r,g) to P for every finite tuple g in I. On the free A-module of the actual wedge-cycle generators of [new-e1-koszul-conormal-cycle-presentation], evaluate each generator by the induced homology map of its specified a(r,g). The kernel of the explicit conormal presentation is contained in the kernel of this explicit homology evaluation. No comparison map is an input or conclusion.

source.place: Lemma 23.6.12, strictly commutative Tor product via free Tate resolutions; Tag 00LS, part (2), comparison homotopies

proof.text: Compute quotient-tensored homology with a free strictly commutative Tate resolution Q. Degree-one lifts of elements of I define classes depending only on I/I^2: differences of lifts are boundaries by exactness; the lift of a product xy can be chosen as x times a lift of y and vanishes after tensoring when x is in I. Additivity and the quotient scalar rule follow from adding and scaling lifts.

Products of degree-one classes are alternating even in characteristic two by strict commutativity. Thus the product assignment respects all additive, balanced, and alternating relations of the exterior conormal. Sending Koszul generators to degree-one lifts gives Koszul-to-Q maps realizing those products.

Compare Q to P. Its composite with each Koszul map is homotopic to the specified augmentation-preserving a(r,g), by [new-r4-koszul-augmentation-lift-homotopy]. Tensoring preserves homotopy and hence the homology evaluations agree. All conormal relations therefore evaluate to zero in P. The monomorphism iCycles makes the actual cycle representatives unambiguous.
